identity.name: PERMANENT MAGNETS LTD.
identity.industry: Specialty Magnetics & Soft-Magnetic Alloys (rare-earth assemblies, electrical contacts/relays, precision alloys)

summary.oneLiner: A small-cap specialty-magnetics maker pivoting from a cyclical legacy base (meters, auto, exports) toward three optionality-rich growth pillars — Alloys (now ramping), Relays (import-substitution, delayed to H2 FY27) and rare-earth magnets via Quantum Magnetics — where execution has chronically lagged guidance and the China rare-earth choke has zeroed FY26 magnet revenue.
summary.business: PML manufactures a wide range of components and assemblies built on core technologies in current sensing, speed and magnetic sensing, magnetic shielding and magnetic assemblies, sold into automotive, energy metering and other industries. It positions itself as a solutions partner rather than a component supplier, bringing design, prototyping and production together under one roof and building customised parts to customer specification. Alongside sensing components it produces specialised alloys (Nickel-Iron, Cobalt, Manganese and Nickel-based) and ZAMAK die-cast parts, and is developing latching relays and, through its subsidiary Quantum Magnetics, a rare earth permanent magnet value chain in India.

Magnetic Sensing: Speed sensing devices using Alnico magnets
Torque and angle sensing assemblies for EPAS/EPS
Relays (under development): Latching Relays (licensed from REL Developments Limited, UK)

currentContext.strengths: Six decades of accumulated expertise in magnets and magnetic assemblies; described as the preferred, and often the only, supplier across its product categories|Multidisciplinary knowledge base spanning metallurgy, mechanical, electrical and electronics engineering, allowing design-to-production solutions under one roof|In-house design, simulation and customer-specific prototyping capability that lets it optimise client designs rather than only build to print|Proprietary process technologies including NADCAP-compliant annealing furnaces, cited as a source of favourable cost structures|Advanced measurement and qualification infrastructure (Koerzimat, BH Loop Plotter, AEC-Q200 lab) supporting stringent customer quality benchmarks and regular customer audits|Broad capability-led portfolio of 350+ actively manufactured SKUs across eight end-industries, reducing dependence on any single technology cycle|AS9100D certification at the alloys facility opening aerospace and defence opportunities|Licensing agreement with REL Developments Limited, UK for Latching Relays, a product worth up to five times the value of its existing shunt and CT basket
currentContext.strategies: Scale up commercial operations across three named growth pillars: Alloys, Relays and Quantum Magnetics, converting existing groundwork into commercial results|Build versatile core capabilities and technologies rather than individual products, so the portfolio stays resilient through technological shifts and addresses a broad market|Grow the Alloys division into a major vertical by scaling commercial production through FY27 and engaging customers in oil and gas, aerospace and other sectors, leveraging AS9100D certification for aerospace and defence entry|Move the metering business up-value into Latching Relays, manufactured under a licensing agreement with REL Developments Limited, UK, a product worth up to five times the value of the existing shunt and CT basket|Localise a neodymium rare earth permanent magnet value chain in India through subsidiary Quantum Magnetics under a joint venture agreement|Widen the automotive and EV customer base and target a broader range of automotive and industrial products, already supplying electric two-wheeler OEMs, to offset Chinese share gains at Western EV manufacturers|Consolidate manufacturing operations into a single, more efficient facility over time on land already acquired
currentContext.expansion: PML's expansion in FY26 centred on three growth projects. In the Alloys division a new furnace was installed in January and commercialised in Q4FY26, running close to optimum capacity for the remainder of the year; the division entered FY27 with better order visibility and growing enquiries from oil & gas, aerospace and industrial customers, supported by AS 9100D:2016 certification. The Relay manufacturing facility, for Latching Relays to be made under a licensing agreement with REL Developments Limited, UK, is largely ready and progressing through testing and customer qualification, with commercial production now expected to commence in H2FY27 (behind the original timeline because customers require extended endurance testing before adopting a new supplier); the facility has been designed with scalable capacity to support future growth in smart metering. Subsidiary Quantum Magnetics, operating under a joint venture agreement to localise a neodymium magnet value chain in India, is advancing Phase 2 implementation covering block cutting, machining and surface treatment, with that next phase of investment expected in Q3FY27 and a long-term ambition of integrated capacity of 5,000 tonnes by FY31. Separately, the Company has acquired land to bring its manufacturing operations together into a single, more efficient facility over time, and states that for FY27 it plans to continue investing in capacity expansion and to pursue incremental growth opportunities.
currentContext.mdna: FY26 recovery was concentrated in the second half, led by the scale-up of the Alloys division and capacity commissioning, with improving exports and steady demand in electricity meter and automotive applications|First half was held back by lower exports, particularly to the United States following interim uncertainty in tariff policy, and by weaker domestic energy meter demand; both improved as the year progressed|Standalone EBITDA margin rose to 17% from 14%, aided by a more favourable product mix and the second-half revenue scale-up|Automotive/EV demand at Western EV manufacturers held at similar levels even as Chinese manufacturers continued to gain share globally|The current transformer (CT) business continued to grow well across the year|Long runway in smart metering: only 65 million of the Government of India's targeted 250 million smart meters under RDSS were installed as of April 2026, supporting the relays opportunity as it commercialises|Consolidated results reflect the early investment phase at subsidiary Quantum Magnetics|Quantum Magnetics could not generate revenue from the existing assemblies business this year because of restrictions on rare earth magnets, which management says strengthens the case for an Indian supply chain|Relays commercialisation is running behind original timelines because customers require extended endurance testing before adopting a new supplier

risks.risk: Export exposure to US trade/tariff policy
risks.note: The MD's letter states the first half of FY26 was held back by lower exports business, particularly to the United States following interim uncertainty in tariff policy, making a material part of the revenue base sensitive to trade-policy shifts outside the Company's control.

risks.risk: Competitive share loss to Chinese manufacturers in EV/automotive
risks.note: PML supplies primarily Western EV manufacturers, where demand held flat while Chinese manufacturers continue to gain share globally; the Company's response is to widen its customer base and product range, so the vertical's growth depends on that diversification succeeding.

risks.risk: Rare earth supply restrictions affecting the magnet assemblies business
risks.note: The Company could not generate revenue from the existing assemblies business at subsidiary Quantum Magnetics this year because of restrictions on rare earth magnets — an external supply-chain constraint that directly removed a revenue stream.

risks.risk: Execution and timeline slippage in the Relays programme
risks.note: Management explicitly acknowledges being behind original timelines on Relays, with commercial ramp-up pushed to H2FY27 because customers require extended endurance testing before adopting a new supplier; the growth case for the metering business rests on this conversion.

risks.risk: Customer concentration and customer-specific demand volatility in domestic energy meters
risks.note: Domestic energy meter demand was softer in the first half due to certain customer-specific factors before recovering later in the year, indicating the segment's volumes can swing on the behaviour of a small number of customers.

risks.risk: Early investment phase drag from the Quantum Magnetics subsidiary
risks.note: Consolidated results reflect the early investment phase at Quantum Magnetics, and further phases of investment are due in Q3FY27, so consolidated profitability will continue to carry the venture's build-out cost ahead of any revenue.

risks.risk: Regulatory/statutory cost changes — new labour codes
risks.note: Standalone net profit growth in FY26 was struck after absorbing a one-time provision relating to the new labour codes, evidencing exposure to changes in statutory employment cost regimes.

risks.risk: Dependence on a government programme for the metering growth runway
risks.note: The relays opportunity is framed around the Government of India's RDSS smart-meter rollout, of which only 65 million of a targeted 250 million meters were installed as of April 2026 — the runway is large but the pace of the addressable market is set by a public programme.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary
segment_detail.body:
- **Alloys**: new furnace installed Jan 2026, commercialized Q4, ran near full util.; product split virgin metal (lower margin, dominant in Q4) vs scrap-route (higher margin); mix to be clearer by Q1-Q2 FY27.
- **Relays**: import-substitution play (largely imported today; PML had one smart-meter customer, now broad-basing). Avg meter value INR 250-300; TAM ~INR 6,500-7,000 cr on 25 cr meter replacement cycle.
- **Quantum Magnetics** (subsidiary): rare-earth magnets; raised $5m ECB; PML contribution ~$5m over ~18 months; Phase 1 (assemblies) done, Phase 2 under implementation.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body:
- No consolidated order-book figure disclosed.
- Alloys: engaging customers in oil & gas (already in commercial production), aerospace, others; oil & gas the near-term ramp driver.
- Relays: customer approvals/testing in progress; production equipment purchase contingent on which orders "click first."
- Rare-earth: long-term 5,000-tonne plant plan; full build-out only by ~FY30-31, revenue potential INR 3,000-4,000 cr at full scale (highly conditional).

guidance.title: Guidance (next quarter / year)
guidance.body:
- FY27 consolidated revenue growth **20-30%** (could exceed on large orders), driven primarily by Alloys; Relays/Quantum additive.
- FY27 EBITDA margin held **~15-18%** (similar to FY26).
- Alloys: FY27 volume **3-4x** of FY26 contribution.
- Relays: commercial ramp from **H2 FY27**; peak FY27 revenue INR 25-50 cr at ~100% util (phased 5m → 10m unit capacity).
- Quantum/rare-earth: Phase 2 (block cutting/machining/surface treatment) in Q3-Q4 FY27; first assembly sales ~Dec FY27, ~INR 10-15 cr in Q4 FY27.
- No FY28/29/30 numeric guidance given (deferred).

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- Rare-earth magnet localization (PLI scheme being evaluated, not yet applied) — large optionality but early and contested.
- Customers shifting heavy-rare-earth → light-rare-earth designs (potential future tailwind for PML).
- Chinese EV makers with Indian collaborations: PML developing products for them; cannot yet sell into China directly.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- FY26 EBITDA 17% (vs 14% FY25) on mix + H2 scale. Q4 15%, down QoQ.
- Virgin-metal alloy sales dilute margin vs scrap-route; near-term mix skewed to virgin metal.
- Guidance keeps margins flat (~15-18%) despite ramp — limited near-term operating leverage signaled.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Increased borrowing limits; consolidated debt rose mainly via $5m ECB for subsidiary capex (standalone debt modest ~INR 20 cr).
- Heavy reinvestment phase across all three pillars + new factory; no dividend/buyback commentary.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: - Candid and measured; explicitly acknowledged delays ("it has been delayed to that extent, yes"). Conservative on guidance, repeatedly hedging on customer-order timing. Tone realistic but credibility dented by repeated commercialization delays and an IR-access complaint.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **Chronic execution slippage** — Relays delayed multiple times (now H2 FY27); investor flagged "very poor show" on commercialization vs prior guidance.
- China rare-earth export curbs → zero magnet revenue FY26; no approvals received.
- EV exposure concentrated in EU/US platforms losing share to Chinese OEMs; no Chinese-EV business.
- Competition in rare-earth (5-6 players + big names planning, PLI-driven) and Alloys.
- Funding mix for large FY27 capex unsettled; consolidated debt rising.
- Poor IR responsiveness flagged by an investor (unanswered meeting requests).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- FY26 "growth" (+13%) is almost entirely an H2/Alloys phenomenon masking a weak H1; rare-earth — the headline optionality — contributed nothing.
- The big consolidated debt jump (INR 15→85 cr feared by an investor) is largely a definitional/ECB artifact, not standalone balance-sheet stress — CFO actively corrected the INR 85 cr figure.
- Relays revenue is a high-uncertainty bet: INR 25-50 cr range at "100% utilization" of a capacity still being phased in, fully dependent on customer adoption speed.
- Light-vs-heavy rare-earth substitution trend is a quiet structural positive PML is positioning for.

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log
qoq_log.body:
- Q4 standalone revenue INR 66 cr (+47% YoY) vs softer H1; FY26 INR 225 cr (+13%).
- Q4 EBITDA margin 15% — up YoY, down QoQ (vs FY26 17%).
- Alloys furnace newly commercialized in Q4 (Jan install) — first quarter of meaningful Alloys contribution.
- Relays timeline pushed again: now H2 FY27 commercial ramp (vs earlier-expected sooner).
- Rare-earth/Quantum: Phase 1 done, Phase 2 now under implementation; first sales pushed to ~Q4 FY27.
- $5m ECB newly raised in subsidiary — consolidated debt up vs prior.
- vs prior call: China-restriction easing expected "by Q3/Jan-Feb" did NOT materialize — no approvals, no magnet sales.
